title: Array Operations & Tricks 🎩
description: Slice, append, remove, and loop over arrays – master the full toolbox.

slides.title: Appending Elements ➕
slides.content:
## Grow Your Array

To add an element to the end of an indexed array:
```bash
arr+=(new_item)
```
This works for both indexed and associative (with a key). For an associative array: `arr[newkey]=value`.

You can also append multiple items at once: `arr+=(a b c)`.

slides.title: Add to an Array
slides.content: Start with two items, then add more:

quizData.question: `arr+=(value)` adds a new element to the beginning of the array.
quizData.explanation: It appends to the end (or next available index).

slides.title: Slicing: Take a Subset 🔪
slides.content:
## `${array[@]:offset:length}`

You can extract a slice of an indexed array:
- `${arr[@]:2}` – all elements starting from index 2.
- `${arr[@]:1:3}` – three elements starting from index 1.

This creates a new list; the original array is unchanged.

slides.title: Slice Demo
slides.content: Get days from the third onward:
slides.codeSnippet:
days=(Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri)
echo "${days[@]:2}"      # Wed Thu Fri
echo "${days[@]:1:2}"   # Tue Wed

quizData.question: What expression extracts the second and third elements from an array `arr`? (index 1 and 2)
quizData.explanation: Offset 1 skips the first element, length 2 grabs two items.

slides.title: Removing Elements 🗑️
slides.content:
## Unset an Index

Use `unset arr[index]` to delete a specific element. The indices after it do **not** shift; a hole remains (sparse array).

To reset the whole array: `unset arr` or `arr=()`.

Be careful with associative arrays: `unset arr[key]` removes that key.

slides.title: Delete an Item
slides.codeSnippet:
fruits=(apple banana cherry)
unset fruits[1]
echo "${fruits[@]}"        # apple cherry
echo "Indexes: ${!fruits[@]}"  # 0 2

slides.title: Testing Existence 🧪
slides.content:
## Check if an Index or Key Exists

For indexed: `[ -n "${arr[idx]+exists}" ]` or `[[ -v arr[idx] ]]` (Bash 4.2+).
For associative, `[[ -v assoc[key] ]]` is the cleanest way.

This is useful to avoid unbound variable errors.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Copy an array: `new_arr=( "${old_arr[@]}" )`. For associative, iterate and assign key by key.
